From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 8 May 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Next-steps: Luminexa POC traffic & success-signal alignment

Hi Sam — great conversation today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into the trial: 

1) Proposed POC scope (2 weeks):
- Ingest a representative subset of your API traffic (you'll share a 24–72h sample)
- Run functional validation (accuracy checks) + performance probes (baseline and burst)
- Measure key success signals and cost estimates

2) Initial workload / traffic profile (please confirm):
- Sustained baseline: ~60 RPS
- Concurrency: ~40 concurrent requests (typical)
- Token lengths: avg ~60 tokens / response; 95th pct ~240 tokens
- Burst behavior: short bursts up to ~500 RPS for 2 minutes (please confirm if you see longer spikes)
- Model: endpoint will call a single generation model (no tool calls in initial run)

3) Success criteria (suggested):
- Functional: agreement rate on eval set (pass/fail) >= 92%
- Performance: p95 latency < 400 ms for baseline traffic; graceful degradation during bursts (no HTTP 5xx above 0.5%)
- Cost: rolling estimate within budget envelope we discuss

4) Deliverables & owners:
- Luminexa: share traffic sample (expected-traffic-sample.jsonl) + procurement contact (Procurement <procure@luminexa.ai>) — action: Sam
- Redwood (Vanessa): finalize POC outline and timeline (attached) — action: me
- Redwood (Aditya): set up probe profiles and run test harness — action: Aditya
- Redwood (Sean): cost/time estimate for Dedicated vs. Hosted run and an A/B fallback plan — action: Sean

5) Timeline proposal:
- May 10: receive traffic sample & procurement contact
- May 12–13: Redwood config + smoke probes
- May 15–26: 2-week POC window
- May 27: readout and next-step decision

Attachments: luminexa-poc-outline.pdf (application/pdf, 42KB); poc-success-metrics.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 18KB)

Please reply with any corrections to the traffic profile above and confirm who will be our procurement contact so Sean can start the commercial paperwork. If the burst profile is higher than noted, please include the observed peak magnitude and duration.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this stood up.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Thanks Vanessa — that recap looks good, a couple small corrections below and we can share the sample by EOD Monday.

Corrections / clarifications:
- Token lengths: our backend shows avg ~45 tokens, p95 ~180 tokens on responses (we saw one workflow with longer outputs but that is not in scope)
- Burst behavior: we've seen short spikes to ~800 RPS but typically for 20–45 seconds (not sustained). The 500 RPS for 2 minutes you propose is fine for probing.
- Concurrency: concurrent open requests can hit ~60 in rare windows; baseline is still closer to 30–40.

Procurement: I'll loop in our procurement alias once you confirm scope. Expect sample: expected-traffic-sample.jsonl (anonymized) and a short README describing peak windows.

Agree with the success signals — we might tighten functional pass to 94% after the first readout, but start with 92% for initial acceptance.

We'll aim to send the sample and the procurement contact by EOD Monday (May 10).

Best,
Sam
Sam Turner
Head of Integrations, Luminexa AI
sam.turner@luminexa.ai | +1 (617) 555-3342
